# Preface {.unnumbered}

This is a small executable textbook. It starts from the transfer equation
and a slab with one opacity, and it ends, four milestones later, with a toy
radiative-transfer calculation that produces a light curve three ways: with
a scalar thermalisation parameter, with an effective redistribution matrix,
and with an explicit atom. Along the way every idea is implemented twice: in
twenty to fifty transparent lines inside a notebook, and once more as a small
reusable function in the `rtedu` package, with a test that states the physics
the function must satisfy.

**What it is not.** Nothing here is publication evidence. The demos teach and
validate concepts; the research code in `revisit_sobolev` (`sobolev/`,
`paper2/phase1/forest_mc.py`, `paper3/redistribution/kernel.py`) implements
the same ideas with real atomic data and controlled physics, and the last
chapter of the book maps every toy object to its production counterpart.

**How it is built.** Every number quoted in the text comes from the
notebooks, through a results file the build regenerates from scratch; every
figure and animation is produced by code from a fixed seed. The eleven-section
template of each chapter is the same: *Question, Theory, Limiting cases,
Numerical model, Demo, Visualization, Validation, What approximation did we
introduce?, How does this map to `revisit_sobolev`?, What would fail if our
assumption were wrong?, Exercises.*

**The four parts.** Part I learns radiative transfer from zero (chapters 0–4)
and ends where a packet finds its next line interaction. Part II asks what
happens to the packet's energy once it has hit an atom (chapters 5–8). Part
III derives the effective model, the redistribution matrix, and asks when it
works (chapters 9–12). Part IV puts everything back into a transport
calculation and bridges to the production code (chapter 13 and the bridge).
All four parts are in this build.
